title: Add delegated trace aggregator and SLA-aware alert coordinator
author: Maya Singh
description: Context: Several tenants reported noisy alert storms during transient kernel queue spikes where token-level cost variance caused many per-route SLO alerts to fire simultaneously. Root cause analysis showed (1) high-cardinality trace fanout from per-shard sampling, (2) duplicated trace fragments across ingest, and (3) lack of tenant-priority weighting in alert scoring. This PR introduces a delegated trace aggregator service plus an SLA-aware alert coordinator to reduce alert churn and provide deterministic cost/latency attribution. Summary of changes: - Add delegated_trace_aggregator service (go) that consumes sampled spans from the observability ingestion stream, performs idempotent coalescing of trace fragments across shards, computes compact fingerprints, and emits aggregated trace rollups at a configurable cadence. The aggregator uses a two-tier reservoir (fast LRU + epoch sketch) to bound memory and prioritize recent, high-cost traces. - Add sla_alert_coordinator (python) that subscribes to aggregated rollups, computes per-invocation alert scores by combining token-cost, latency percentile deltas, and tenant SLA weight, and emits suppression or escalate decisions via the alerting bus. It implements a decay window to avoid repeated re-alerting on the same root cause. - Telemetry: new metrics (delegated_trace_coalesced_count, delegated_trace_rollup_latency_ms, sla_alert_score, sla_alert_suppressed_total, rollup_memory_pressure_gauge) + tags for tenant_id, route, model_family, kernel_bucket. - Dashboards: add compact rollup panel (rollup velocity / coalesced ratio), SLA score heatmap by tenant and route, and alert-suppression timeline. - Alert tuning: new rule templates that consult sla_alert_score and suppress low-priority alerts when a correlated cluster is already open; added knob for per-tenant override (SRE console). - Deployment and ops: helm chart changes to observability-pack, k8s HPA hints for aggregator, and a feature flag `observability.delegated_aggregator.enabled` with canary rollout strategy. Motivation: coalescing reduces cardinality and query cost while providing a single source of truth for invocation-level cost attribution; SLA-aware scoring reduces alert noise and helps oncall focus on meaningful regressions. Rollout plan: 1) Internal canary in staging with 5 tenants for 48h, monitor rollup latency and memory pressure; 2) opt-in beta for high-volume tenants; 3) gradual default-on rollout with runtime knob. Backwards compatibility: aggregator emits rollups alongside raw spans; consumers can opt-in. Tests & benchmarks: - Unit tests for coalescing logic and fingerprint stability - Integration test that simulates cross-shard fragment duplication (passes) - Load bench: aggregated rollups reduced trace cardinality by ~73% on a production-shaped replay and increased CPU on aggregator by ~12% (within SLO). Related: ENG-4827 (ticket), SRE-231 on alert fatigue. Links: design doc (internal/observability/delegated-aggregator.md), dashboard JSONs in dashboards/observability/rollups/*.
